title: Bolt a sagging garden gate shut: lift its free end to line the barrel bolt up, slide it home, drop the handle in
context: Garden, yard, side-passage and paddock gates are bolted shut every day, and once a gate's hinges wear its free end drops a few millimetres, so its barrel bolt no longer meets the keeper on the post: slid across, it only butts against the keeper. Bolting such a gate takes two hands working together: one lifts the gate's free end, bearing its weight, and holds it so that the bolt lines up with the keeper within its few millimetres of play, while the other slides the bolt across into the keeper until it stops; then the bolt's handle is turned down into the notch at the end of its slot, so the bolt cannot slide back. Lift too little or too much and the bolt stops against the keeper; let the gate drop before the bolt is in and it has to be lifted again.
setup: Positions in mm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table top (x forward, y to the robot's left, z up). Gate post: grey timber, 90 x 90 mm, x 300 to 390, y -130 to -40, cut off 160 mm up, fixed, with a 20 x 30 mm gate-stop batten on its +y side behind the gate. Gate: the bolt-height band of the latch end of a shut, boarded western red cedar garden gate, its face (toward the robot) at x 300, 45 mm thick, its free edge at y -30 (10 mm from the post) and its hinges 900 mm away at y 870 (off the table). Shown: a 45 x 70 mm stile (y -30 to 40) and lock rail (to y 330), 40 to 110 mm up, with 20 mm infill boards above the rail to 180 mm; 0.72 kg with the bolt's plate. It hangs on its worn hinges 7 mm low at the bolt (it can be lifted up to 16 mm). Barrel bolt (black steel, 150 mm): backplate 150 x 40 x 2 mm on the lock rail, y -25 to 125; a 12 mm zinc bolt, 150 mm long, its axis 11.5 mm in front of the gate (x 288.5) and 75 mm up when the gate hangs true, drawn back with its end at y -27; it slides 45 mm toward the post. Its handle, a 4 mm stem with a 14 mm black knob 33 mm out from the bolt's axis, sticks out toward the robot through the barrel's slot at y 105, resting 13 degrees down on the slot's lip; the lip has a 10 mm notch at the end of the bolt's travel (y 55 to 65). Keeper: a 3 mm steel staple on the post's face, y -75 to -45, with an 18 mm square opening centred 75 mm up on the bolt's line (3 mm play all round the bolt).
scoring: Measured with a ruler and a photo: the bolt end's height against the centre of the keeper's opening, and how far the bolt's end is past the keeper's mouth (it stops at 27 mm). 1.0 if it is at least 25 mm past the mouth with the handle turned down at least 70 degrees into its notch, for 1 s in a row with the bolt still (its end moving under 1 mm); 0.75 if it was ever at least 25 mm past the mouth; 0.5 if ever at least 5 mm past it; 0.25 if the bolt's end was ever within 3 mm (up or down) of the opening's centre (the gate lifted to line it up); else 0.
reset_notes: Turn the handle up, slide the bolt back until it stops, and let the gate down onto its hinges' stop.
fidelity: Rigid boxes and cylinders at real size. Only the gate's latch end at bolt height is modelled (360 x 140 mm) on a hinge 900 mm away, so it takes about 11 N to lift where the demo holds it, less than a whole gate would. Hinge wear is a stop 7 mm low. Bolt and handle run on frictionless joints with light damping; the handle drops by its weight into the notch. Friction 0.6 (bolt 0.3). No contact force cap.
